parsed.elsewhere_quote:
Binary expansion says that the subset sums of (9) are exactly, and uniquely,

\[
0,\delta,2\delta,\ldots,(2^{n+1}-1)\delta=1.
\]

Therefore \(\Gamma=\delta\). Xiang has at most \(n=(n+1)-1\) cuts, so the lower half of the refinement lemma gives \(D\ge\delta\) for every one of his marking choices.
parsed.explanation: Partial sums of δ,2δ,4δ,…,2^nδ are δ,3δ,7δ,…,(2^j−1)δ, so the parenthetical "marks are 2^j δ" is indeed a misprint (only j=1 coincides). But the lower bound never uses the mark coordinates: display (9) fixes the interval lengths δ,2δ,…,2^nδ, binary uniqueness gives Γ=δ, and the refinement lemma's lower half yields D≥δ against every Xiang reply with ≤n cuts. The marks are plainly distinct interior points for these lengths. Hence L3.3 stands; only the symbol 2^j needs to become 2^j−1.
